research.statement:
# CedarWorks Labs company knowledge
Fictional company knowledge base for ProofApply testing. Supplied knowledge, not a live web page. Illustrative site: https://cedarworks.example. The .example domain is not an actual employer website.
## Product context
CedarWorks Labs creates scheduling and booking software for small organizations. Its frontend team prioritizes clear forms, visible error states and interfaces that work with a keyboard.
## Engineering context
The frontend team values readable TypeScript, component tests and collaborative Git workflows. Docker appears as a preferred qualification in the fictional frontend opening. Some separate platform roles use Kubernetes. These company facts do not imply any candidate has those skills.
## Research question supported by this source
Which parts of a campus booking-interface project are relevant to the frontend opening? Form design, REST integration, error handling, tests, keyboard access and collaborative changes align with the product/team description.
No company headcount, salary, growth, customer counts or employment outcomes are supplied. Do not invent them.
research.uncertainty: Supplied knowledge; no live site verification.

claims.text: Computer Science student with experience developing frontend interfaces using React and TypeScript. Proficient in integrating REST APIs, implementing accessible form components, and maintaining code quality through automated unit testing and collaborative Git workflows.

evidence.exact_excerpt: Mira built the room-availability view and booking-form screens using React and TypeScript.
Mira connected these screens to the team's existing REST endpoints for listing rooms and creating booking requests.
Mira authored 18 Vitest unit tests for the booking form's validation and error states.
Mira added visible keyboard focus states, associated input labels and accessible inline error text to the booking form.
Mira used Git branches and pull requests to submit her changes.
